stem: A newspaper surveyed 400 randomly selected readers about whether they prefer to read the news online or in print. Each reader chose exactly one option. The incomplete table summarizes the results. If one of the surveyed readers who prefer print is selected at random, what is the probability that the reader is 18 to 34 years old?

figure.title: Preferred news format by age group

explanation.A: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{48}{400}\): it divides by all 400 readers instead of only the 144 readers who prefer print.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{48}{180}\), the probability that a reader 18 to 34 prefers print: the condition is reversed.
explanation.C: Correct. 48 of the 144 readers who prefer print are 18 to 34, and \(\frac{48}{144} = \frac{1}{3}\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(\frac{96}{144}\), the probability that a print reader is 35 or older.

verify:
r = figure['rows']
young_print = int(r[0][3]) - int(r[0][1])
print_total = young_print + int(r[1][2])
p = Rational(young_print, print_total)
assert int(r[2][3]) - int(r[0][3]) == 220
assert p == Rational(1, 3)
assert value(choices[answer]) == p
assert all(value(choices[k]) != p for k in choices if k != answer)
